Answer: F
Reason: The provided images are axial CT scans (not chest X-rays) showing a large right pleural effusion and right lung atelectasis/compression, with a prominent vascular structure in the right lower lobe suggestive of an anomalous vein draining into the IVC/right atrium; this constellation is characteristic of Scimitar syndrome (a congenital vascular anomaly), making Option F the best fit despite the modality discrepancy in the question stem. Options A, C, D, and E describe findings inconsistent with the unilateral right-sided pathology and specific vascular anatomy seen, while Option B incorrectly attributes the findings to Scimitar syndrome but includes "enlarged heart shadow" which is less specific than the vascular anomaly description in F for this classic presentation.
